To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Neu receptor tyrosine kinases are overexpressed in 20 to30% of human breast cancers and that Neu-induced mammary tumorgenesis can be inhibited by the Rap-1A GTPase.

Neu (Erb B2) induces breast cancers in transgenic mice by activating the Ras and Rap signaling cascades, that the adapter protein Grb2 and the adaptor protein Shc play distinct roles in Neu (Erd B2) induced breast cancers, and that Neu (ErdB 2) induced breast tumors in transgenic mice metastasize to the lungs.
the Neu tyrosine kinase can transform mammary epithelial cells and induce mammary cancers by recruiting Grb2 or Shc adapter proteins to distinct tyrosine autophosphoryl sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which ErbB-1, ErbB-3, and ErbB-4 cooperate with Neu (Erb B-2 or HER2) to induce mammary tumorigensis.
the mechanisms that regulate cell proliferation and survival.

the molecular mechanisms by which the ErbB-3 and ErbB-4 receptors function in the context of other ErbB receptors and the ErbB receptor ligands, and how these interactions influence the growth and differentiation of mammary epithelial cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Neu receptor can activate a number of signaling pathways and that the relative contribution of these pathways in tumorigenesis is dependent upon the specific Neu receptor mutant.
Grb2 plays a critical role in ErbB2-induced mammary tumourigenesis, and that Shc may also be involved, although to a lesser extent.
the Neu receptor tyrosine kinases are oncogenes that induce mammary cancers by activating distinct downstream signaling pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Grb2 adapter protein is a critical mediator for Neu-induced mammary tumourigenesis and that Shc plays an important, but less critical, role in Neu-induced mammary cancer.

Neu-induced mammary tumorgenesis is a multistep process, and the Neu receptor can activate several different signaling cascades that may be differentially involved in different aspects of the tumorgenesis process.
Neu (Erb B2 or HER- 2) induced mammary tumorigeneses are mediated by the adaptor proteins Shc and Grb2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Grb2 adapter protein is required for ErbB- 2-induced tumorigenesis, whereas Shc is not.
the Neu receptor can activate multiple downstream pathways and that these pathways play distinct roles in Neu-mediated tumorigenesis.
the ErbB-3 receptor is a major player in the development of breast cancer, particularly in the metastatic spread of breast cancer.
